routine.name: love-tap improvement loop
routine.delivery: two hops: the Routine wakes a persistent orchestrator, which spawns a fresh worker per firing with create_session and the repository attached
routine.worker_prompt: loop/WORKER_PROMPT.md, referenced by the Routine so it can be corrected here rather than in a Routine nobody can read the history of
routine.why_two_hops: A session a Routine mints directly gets sources: [], and the egress proxy injects a push credential only for a session's attached sources, so every git push returns 403. Firing 0 cloned the repo -- readable, the repo is public -- worked seven minutes, committed a76f8e3, could not push it, and lost it when the container was reclaimed. Two probe firings then established that a fired session cannot attach the repository to itself either. create_session can, through source_url and outcome_branch, and a worker created that way pushed on its first attempt.
traps_paid_for_already: list_triggers reports last_run SUCCEEDED for a firing that achieved nothing: it records delivery, not accomplishment. A commit on origin is the only proof a firing did anything.

update_trigger has no persistent_session_id parameter -- only create_trigger does. Passing it to update_trigger is silently ignored, so a rebinding needs the Routine recreated. Read persist_session back rather than trusting the call.
create_session cannot make a child more permissive than its parent, so an orchestrator must be created from a session that is not in plan mode, or it inherits plan and stalls for ever.
